info.name: Xibra Platform API
info.description:
Postman collection for the verified endpoints of **xibra-api** (Batches 1-6): health, authentication, Owner-only invitation management, public invitation onboarding, and Telegram identity linking.

## Setup

1. Start the API: `php artisan serve` inside `D:\Xibra-Platform\xibra-api` (default base URL `http://127.0.0.1:8000`).
2. In this collection's **Variables** tab, set `owner_password` to the value of `XIBRA_OWNER_PASSWORD` from `xibra-api/.env`.
3. Run the collection in order (Collection Runner) - later requests depend on variables captured by earlier ones:
   - `POST /auth/login` captures `access_token`
   - `POST /invitations` captures `invitation_id`, `invitation_code`, `invitation_token`
   - `POST /invitations/redeem` captures `onboarding_session_token`
   - `POST /onboarding/complete` captures `onboarding_member_token` and `member_access_token`
   - `POST /telegram/link-codes` captures `telegram_link_code`; signed bot requests build their signature in a pre-request script
4. Set `bot_secret` to `XIBRA_BOT_SECRET` from `xibra-api/.env`. `bot_key_id` must match `XIBRA_BOT_KEY_ID` (default `xibra-bot-v1`).

## Notes

- The response contract for every endpoint is `{success, message, code, data, meta}` (`docs/api/conventions.md` 5). Clients should branch on `code`, not `message`.
- A full run **creates one real invitation and revokes it** in the Invitations folder. The Onboarding folder **creates one real Member account and one redeemed invitation**; nothing is deleted. Skip the Onboarding folder if you do not want additional live accounts.
- The Onboarding complete request derives a unique username and email per run (`member_<timestamp>`), so repeated runs do not collide.
- The Telegram folder unlinks first, links a random test Telegram ID to the authenticated account, then unlinks again. It is repeatable and leaves no linked identity behind.
- `bot_secret` is a live credential. Never export, share, or commit the collection while it is filled in.
- Login rate limiting (5/min per identifier, 20/min per IP) and onboarding rate limiting (10/min per IP) are intentionally **not** exercised: triggering them would lock the run for a minute.
- The member-forbidden check (403) uses the `member_access_token` captured by the Onboarding folder. If that folder is skipped, the variable is empty and the check gracefully falls back to asserting 401 UNAUTHENTICATED.
- Invitation codes and tokens are returned exactly once, in the create response. The API stores only hashes.
- All requests send `Content-Type: application/json` and expect JSON responses regardless of the Accept header.

request.description: Public liveness probe. Expects HTTP 200 with code HEALTHY.

Authenticate with any of the three identifiers (username, email, phone) in the `identifier` field. On success, captures `data.token` into the `access_token` collection variable. Rate limited: 5/min per identifier, 20/min per IP.

exec: pm.test("owner role is present", () => pm.expect(res.data.user.roles.map(r => r.name)).to.include("owner"));
pm.test("no password material in the user payload", () => pm.expect(res.data.user).to.not.have.property("password"));

request.description: The authenticated identity, resolved from the bearer token only. Expects HTTP 200 with code USER_RETRIEVED.
Revokes the token used for the request. Expects HTTP 200 with code LOGGED_OUT.
Repeats /auth/me with the token revoked by the previous request. Expects HTTP 401 with code UNAUTHENTICATED — proof that logout really revoked the token.
Logs in again so the later folders have a valid bearer token. Captures a fresh access_token.

Paginated invitation listing, newest first. Requires the `invitations.manage` permission (owner role). Pagination metadata lives in `meta` per docs §10: current_page, per_page, total, last_page. `per_page` max is 100.

Creates an invitation and returns its one-time secrets. `expires_in_hours` is optional (default 24, bounds 1–72), `role` is optional (default member, `owner` is rejected), `note` is optional (max 1000 chars). The code and token in `data.secrets` are the only copies that will ever exist — the database stores hashes. Each run of this request creates a real invitation; the run revokes it later in this folder.

pm.test("one-time code has the documented format", () => {
pm.test("no secret hashes in the invitation payload", () => {

request.description: Single invitation. The `status` is the effective one: an overdue pending invitation reports `expired` even before the hourly sweeper materialises it. Unknown ids are concealed with a 404.
Revokes an unused (pending) invitation. Revoked invitations can never be redeemed. Expects HTTP 200 with code INVITATION_REVOKED.

exec: pm.test("status is revoked with a revoker recorded", () => {

request.description: Repeats the revoke on the now-revoked invitation. Only pending invitations can be revoked: expects HTTP 409 with code INVITATION_NOT_REVOKABLE.
Creates a dedicated pending invitation for the onboarding flow and captures its one-time code. Uses the Owner token from the Auth folder.

exec: pm.test("invitation is pending with the member role", () => {

request.description: Validates the invitation code and opens a short-lived (15 minute, single-use) onboarding session. Returns the raw session token exactly once; the database stores only its hash. Expects HTTP 201 with code ONBOARDING_SESSION_CREATED.

exec: pm.test("role and invitation expiry are exposed, internals are not", () => {

request.description: Validates the single-use onboarding session and identity, creates an active Member account, marks the invitation redeemed, consumes every session for it, and returns the first Sanctum token. The username and email are made unique per run. Expects HTTP 201 with code ACCOUNT_CREATED. NOTE: this creates a real account.

exec: pm.test("account is active with the member role", () => {

request.description: Resolves the newly onboarded Member from its returned token. Expects HTTP 200 with code USER_RETRIEVED and the member role.
Authorization boundary for the freshly onboarded Member: invitation management requires `invitations.manage`. Expects HTTP 403 with code FORBIDDEN.
Invitation endpoints without a token. Expects HTTP 401 with code UNAUTHENTICATED.

Authorization boundary: a valid Member token must receive HTTP 403 with code FORBIDDEN. The token is captured by the Onboarding folder; if that folder was skipped, the variable is empty and this falls back to asserting 401 UNAUTHENTICATED.
Unknown invitation ids are concealed as a plain 404. Expects code NOT_FOUND.

Invitations can never assign the owner role — the owner account is exclusively provisioned by the bootstrap seeder. Expects HTTP 422 with a specific message in meta.errors.role, and no invitation is created.

exec: pm.test("owner role is explicitly rejected", () => pm.expect(res.meta.errors.role).to.include("The owner role cannot be assigned through an invitation."));

request.description: Page size is capped at 100. Expects HTTP 422 with meta.errors.per_page.
Field-level validation failures return HTTP 422 with the errors in meta.errors.
Unmatched API routes still return the standard JSON envelope. Expects HTTP 404 with code NOT_FOUND.

Removes any Telegram link left by an earlier run so the folder is repeatable, and generates a fresh random Telegram user ID for the run. Uses the collection bearer token (Owner by default). A missing link is not an error.

Issues a one-time 10-minute link code for the authenticated user. The plain code is returned once; only its HMAC hash is stored. Issuing a new code expires the previous one. Rate limited to 5/min per user. Expects HTTP 201 with code TELEGRAM_LINK_CODE_ISSUED.

exec: pm.test("code uses the unambiguous display format", () => pm.expect(res.data.code).to.match(/^[A-HJ-NP-Z2-9]{5}-[A-HJ-NP-Z2-9]{5}$/));

request.description: The authenticated user's own link state before linking. Expects HTTP 200 with linked=false and no identity.

Trusted bot endpoint. The pre-request script signs the exact body with HMAC-SHA256 (method, path, timestamp, nonce, body hash) using bot_secret. The telegram_user_id is trusted because the request is signed by the bot. Expects HTTP 201 with code TELEGRAM_LINKED.

exec: const body = JSON.stringify({ code: code, telegram_user_id: telegramUserId, telegram_username: pm.collectionVariables.get('telegram_test_username') });
pm.test("the signed Telegram ID is linked", () => pm.expect(res.data.identity.telegram_user_id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("telegram_test_user_id"))));
pm.test("the username is stored without the @ prefix", () => pm.expect(res.data.identity.telegram_username).to.eql("xibra_e2e"));
pm.test("the code owner is the authenticated account", () => pm.expect(res.data.user.username).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("owner_username")));

request.description: Proves that service endpoints require the HMAC signature, not a user token or an open route. Expects HTTP 401 with code SERVICE_UNAUTHENTICATED.

Replays the already consumed code with a different Telegram ID. Signed, but the code is single-use. Expects HTTP 409 with code TELEGRAM_LINK_CODE_CONSUMED. This also counts as one failed attempt against the per-Telegram throttle.

exec: const body = JSON.stringify({ code: code, telegram_user_id: telegramUserId });

request.description: Confirms the authenticated account sees only its own link and the normalized Telegram handle. Expects HTTP 200 with linked=true.

exec: pm.test("the identity matches the signed request", () => pm.expect(res.data.identity.telegram_user_id).to.eql(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get("telegram_test_user_id"))));

request.description: Removes the authenticated account link and records a telegram.unlinked audit event. Expects HTTP 200 with code TELEGRAM_UNLINKED.
Confirms the link was removed. Expects HTTP 200 with linked=false and identity=null.
